review_scope: Independent exact-URL support and claim-scope review of assigned account1 citation proposals only; no canonical edits, Neon calls, DDL, or DML.
review_method: Read the frozen packet and account1 proposal/source mappings; checked exact source URLs with direct Firecrawl retrieval or indexed source text and recorded access limits.

evidence: The exact NEA article, published October 4, 2024, describes Project 2025 as a blueprint and says it calls for ending Head Start and universal free school meals. The proposed text attributes the proposals to NEA and expressly disclaims implementation, current program status, and the draft reach figures. The CHN URL from the older draft is not relied upon.
scope_or_access_limit: No issue in the supported claim; NEA is an advocacy organization’s description of the plan, not an implementation record.

evidence: Reuters’ exact October 9 URL and the Times of Israel full-text arrangement support the first-phase ceasefire/hostage-prisoner exchange framework; Axios reports Israeli cabinet approval of the initial arrangement. The corrected title and claim stay on the first phase and do not assert a final comprehensive peace agreement or that Israel and Hamas signed every instrument.
scope_or_access_limit: The Reuters page has subsequent reporting/update material; the proposed first-phase scope is corroborated by the dated arrangement text and cabinet-approval report.

evidence: The mapped Los Angeles Times report attributes the 2018 NSC global-health-security reorganization to John Bolton. The exact TIME report quotes an administration official saying related responsibilities were absorbed into another directorate. The corrected title is about the standalone directorate; the mapping rejects a causal claim that the change caused COVID-19 failures.
scope_or_access_limit: The continuity statement is an attributed administration response, not independently verified reassignment evidence; proposal preserves attribution.

evidence: The exact Reuters report maps the State Department statement to Trump’s direction to end FY2017 and FY2018 foreign-assistance programs for El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras. AP’s exact report says the State Department would work with Congress to suspend 2017/2018 payments and describes steps to cut aid; the Washington Post URL supports the March 30 announcement. Proposed wording is limited to the specified programs and stated action, and disclaims ending all aid, immediate cancellation of every account, or a permanent cutoff.
scope_or_access_limit: The AP describes suspension/payment steps; it does not establish that all appropriated funds were finally or permanently cancelled. The account1 draft discloses this boundary. The older CNBC URL and AP topic hub are correctly dropped.

evidence: The exact DOJ warrant URL was independently fetched as a one-page PDF (HTTP 200). It names Thomas K. Ford, states “A FULL AND UNCONDITIONAL PARDON,” identifies the Southern District of Illinois conviction under 18 U.S.C. §1001 and 30 U.S.C. §820, and lists the April 10, 2003 probation, $2,000 fine, and $125 assessment. The proposed text avoids asserting the warrant explains the underlying conduct or pardon rationale.
scope_or_access_limit: The packet notes the DOJ PDF itself had not previously been fetched; this cross-review fetched the exact URL successfully. The warrant still supplies no motive or narrative of conduct.

evidence: The exact AP URL’s indexed article text identifies at least 16 Epstein-related files no longer accessible from the DOJ public webpage less than a day after posting, including an image with Trump, Epstein, Melania Trump, and Ghislaine Maxwell. AP also says the government had offered no explanation or public notice at report time. The proposal limits the event to the public webpage and explicitly disclaims destruction, custody removal, and Trump direction.
scope_or_access_limit: This is AP’s report of public webpage availability at a particular time; it does not establish what happened to underlying government records.

evidence: An indexed result for the exact DNYUZ URL contains the matching March 4, 2026 syndicated “Four Questions About What’s Next in Texas” text and the excerpt that Trump said he would endorse soon and ask the other candidate to leave. The exact Texas Tribune article reports the Cornyn–Paxton Senate runoff and Talarico’s Democratic nomination. The proposal labels the NYT item analysis, not a Trump action, says only part of the four-question framing is accessible, and rejects a later endorsement/outcome. Direct Firecrawl retrieval of the DNYUZ URL rendered a generic DNYUZ page rather than that archived article, so this pass relies only on the URL-matched indexed excerpt, not an asserted complete article read.
scope_or_access_limit: The claim is supported only to the excerpt’s scope. The direct-render inconsistency and NYT 403 are disclosed; no later Trump endorsement is evidenced.

evidence: The exact UPI archive report says Trump Castle admitted that Fred Trump’s $3.5 million casino-chip transaction was an unlawful loan to the casino and agreed to a $30,000 penalty; it notes the proposed settlement still required Casino Control Commission approval. The congressional hearing PDF is contextual. Proposed text keeps the subject as Trump Castle and a casino loan, and does not claim a direct personal cash transfer to Donald Trump.
scope_or_access_limit: Keep “agreed to” distinct from final regulatory approval; the UPI report itself notes approval was pending.

evidence: The Knesset’s official press release says Netanyahu’s 37th government was sworn in on December 29, 2022; Reuters reports the coalition’s 63 of 120 votes. Neither mapped source documents a Trump/Kushner relationship, intervention, or consequence. Exclusion from a Trump-specific set is therefore consistent with the verified facts and the proposal’s stated scope.
scope_or_access_limit: The Israeli political event is sourced; the exclusion concerns dataset scope, not a finding that the event did not occur.

evidence: The exact AP report describes Ivanka Trump’s deposition in the D.C. attorney general’s inaugural-fund inquiry and quotes her counsel’s fair-market-rate explanation. The mapped ABC report is the event-specific deposition source. The proposal states the deposition/inquiry and attributed explanation, and explicitly rejects perjury, lying under oath, or any finding of false testimony.
scope_or_access_limit: The AP citation supports the attributed response and inquiry context, not what Ivanka said under oath; no such testimony details are asserted.

evidence: The exact American Presidency Project archive reproduces Trump’s August 20, 2025 post: “We will not approve wind or farmer destroying Solar.” This verifies the date and statement, but not a permitting ban or what projects are covered. The corrected medium and long retain the attribution and disclaim implementation. The corrected short (“wind or solar projects that harm farms”) can be read as applying the farm-damage qualifier to wind too, changing the post’s ambiguous “wind or farmer destroying Solar” wording.
scope_or_access_limit: Revise the short to attribute the exact statement without resolving its grammar, e.g. “Trump wrote that the U.S. would not approve wind or ‘farmer destroying’ solar projects.” No specific permit outcome is sourced.

evidence: The exact Washington Post article (July 6, 2026) says the temporary organization’s charter was expected to terminate July 4 and that the DOGE Service marked what it said was the end of its official work “over Independence Day.” This supports the short/medium/long attribution and reported timing. The proposed title says the official work ended “on July 4,” conflating the charter date with the service’s less exact report of work ending over the holiday.
scope_or_access_limit: Revise title to say “over Independence Day” or “around July 4.” The article does not show all DOGE-related activity across agencies ceased.

evidence: The exact AG-hosted PDF returns HTTP 200 and contains the Iowa fundraiser amounts, but it is a New York Supreme Court motion-to-dismiss opinion, not the AG petition itself. The opinion recounts that the petition alleged the fundraiser raised $5.6 million and $2.823 million was donated to the Foundation. That supports the attributed allegation, but the source mapping misidentifies the linked document as the primary petition. The AG release and NPR URL concern a separate 2019 $2 million court order, not the fundraiser proceeds.
scope_or_access_limit: Keep the alleged fundraiser total separate from the 2019 order. Cite the actual petition or identify the linked document as a court opinion summarizing the AG petition; do not label the allegations as judicial findings.

evidence: The exact TIME article on NSC reorganization covers the 2018 global-health-security unit change; the exact TIME follow-up quotes an administration official that similar responsibilities remained under a different directorate. The corrected title/claim describe reorganization and attribute continuity, while disclaiming a demonstrated causal link to COVID-response failures.
scope_or_access_limit: Continuity is an official’s attributed account. Keep this record distinct from entry-674, which specifically attributes the reorganization to Bolton.

evidence: The exact NBC URL reports the August 12, 2024 live Trump–Musk X discussion and its immigration/technology content. The exact AP URL resolves to AP’s “NOT REAL NEWS” roundup and includes the 2023 fact-check that a $2,200 monthly federal payment claim about undocumented immigrants was false. The draft records the documented conversation, uses AP only as earlier-rumor context, and explicitly says neither source establishes alleged 2024 posts, amplification, campaign use, or audience reach.
scope_or_access_limit: AP is context for an earlier 2023 rumor and does not prove a 2024 Trump/Musk post or amplification.
